b08.h2: 2. What the Service lets you do

b10.p: Test contributions are handled by a Soroban smart contract with the following behaviour: all-or-nothing funding, payout to the campaign only after its deadline, contributions capped at the campaign target, and balances recorded in the contract. No transferable token is issued.

b12.p: Blockallisto is being designed against the compliance surfaces of established EU crowdfunding platforms. b13.p: None of this exists today. The list above is indicative design direction drawn from our research corpus, not a specification: details, thresholds and whole features may change with design work and legal advice. Nothing in this section is a commitment to a launch date or a licence.

b00.notice: Testnet prototype privacy notice, updated 3 November 2026. This describes actual account processing; it is not legal advice or evidence of regulatory authorisation. No real-money operations are enabled.

b02.p: Nuno Ribeiro is the data controller responsible for personal data processed by the Blockallisto testnet prototype. Contact for privacy requests: blockallisto@gmail.com. Blockallisto is a project name, not a claim of a registered company. Fictional company particulars on other DEMO legal templates do not identify the controller for account data.

b04.p: Email/password registration stores your normalized email address, a salted scrypt password hash, account identifier, preferred email language, verification status, timestamps and failed-login/lockout records in the community database. We do not store your password in plain text. Verification and reset tokens are hashed and single-use: verification links expire after 24 hours and reset links after one hour. An email account receives an internal public-key identifier; its generated private key is discarded. This does not give it a wallet capable of signing blockchain transactions.

b05.p: Wallet sign-in remains optional and uses a single-use signed challenge valid for five minutes. When a configured social sign-in provider is available, we store its provider name, stable subject identifier, verified email if returned, and login timestamps; we do not automatically merge accounts by email. New social registration may remain restricted separately from email/password registration. Your email is not used as a public comment author label.

b06.p: Session tokens are hashed on the server; the browser keeps the session token in local storage. Sessions last up to 30 days and can be revoked. If you enable an authenticator second factor, its seed is encrypted server-side and recovery codes are stored as hashes. Password reset revokes sessions and pending second-factor login tickets but does not remove an enrolled second factor.

b07.p: Account records, email credentials and optional second-factor data currently have no automatic account-deletion timer. Expired tokens stop working at expiry, but expiry does not guarantee immediate removal of their stored records. There is no self-service account-deletion tool yet. Ask blockallisto@gmail.com for access, correction or deletion; requests are reviewed against security and legal obligations. Provider logs and backups may have separate retention.

b08.p: Comments (public-key identifier, optional display name, text, campaign and timestamp) are public. The latest 100 per campaign are displayed; hidden comments are deleted after 30 days. Support/feedback tickets, issuer applications and notifications are private to the account and authorised operator roles and are deleted after 90 days by the application cleanup rules. Avoid sensitive personal information in free-text fields.

b10.p: Connecting a wallet or preparing test contributions records public wallet keys, campaign identifiers, amounts, transaction envelopes, hashes, status and timestamps in the safety journal. Unsigned preparations expire after 24 hours; final transactions are pruned after 30 days. Unresolved signed transactions remain until resolved and signed envelopes are scrubbed after finality. Public Stellar testnet records cannot be erased by us. Wallet secret keys stay in your wallet.

b11.p: Theme, language and session choices use browser local storage. Hosting providers process IP addresses and request metadata. Application rate limiting and IP-reputation caching use IP addresses in transient memory; application diagnostics use aggregate counters rather than raw-IP logs. Provider infrastructure logs and backup retention are separate. We do not use advertising trackers or newsletter mailing lists.

b13.p: Render hosts the app in Frankfurt and Neon hosts its Postgres data. Brevo receives recipient email addresses and verification/reset email content and processes delivery metadata. Cloudflare Turnstile processes browser/device signals and challenge tokens for bot checks; server validation may include the client IP. After a successful bot check, ipapi.is receives the client IP for abuse-reputation assessment. Reputation is initially observation-only; VPN, proxy or Tor status alone is not a blocking reason. Provider errors or lookup-budget exhaustion may reduce this layer; CAPTCHA, rate limits and mail budgets are separate safeguards.

b14.p: Where social sign-in is enabled, the chosen identity provider processes that authentication under its own terms. Stellar testnet is public and global. GitHub hosts source code, not the account database. Security and email providers may process data outside the EEA; do not assume every processor is EU-only. Their current policies and applicable safeguards govern their own processing: https://www.brevo.com/legal/privacypolicy/ ; https://www.cloudflare.com/privacypolicy/ ; https://ipapi.is/privacy.html ; https://ipapi.is/terms.html .

b16.p: Data is used to provide the requested prototype account and community features, verify account access, answer support requests and protect the service against abuse. These operational and security purposes rely on legitimate interests under Article 6(1)(f) GDPR, subject to your rights and the assessment required by law. This notice does not certify compliance or replace legal review. We do not sell account data or use it for advertising.

b17.p: You can request access, correction, deletion, restriction, portability or object to processing by writing to blockallisto@gmail.com. You may complain to the Portuguese CNPD or your competent supervisory authority. Public blockchain records cannot be deleted by the operator. The prototype is not directed at children. Identity-document/KYC collection, live investment offerings, fiat payments and real-money operations are not enabled. Any later change requires a new notice before that processing starts.

b02.h2: Read this first: today's demo involves no real money

b03.p: Blockallisto is currently a prototype on the Stellar testnet. All contributions use test tokens with no monetary value. You cannot lose real money on this demo, and nothing on it is a real investment opportunity.

b04.p: The warnings below explain the risks that would apply to the kind of investing Blockallisto demonstrates - crowdfunding into real-world assets through crypto-asset infrastructure. They are published now so that the risk conversation is part of the product from day one.

b06.p: Investing in crowdfunding projects - whether in real-world assets such as property or businesses, or through crypto-assets and tokens - is high risk. You could lose all of the money you invest. Such investments are typically not covered by deposit-guarantee schemes or investor-compensation schemes.

b07.p: Never invest money you cannot afford to lose. For a sense of scale, the reference platforms in our research corpus carry concrete diversification guidance: CONDA's risk-warnings page advises investing no more than about 10% of your freely available funds in this asset class, and the standard Austrian crowdfunding investor sheet (AltFG regime, observed on dagobertinvest) warns against investing more than 10% of net assets. This is the observed risk-communication practice of established platforms, cited as a reference point - it is not a rule of law that applies to this demo, and not a guarantee that any percentage is safe for your situation. Spreading a smaller amount across several projects reduces, but never removes, the risk of total loss.

ul.i00: Capital loss. The project you back may fail, underperform or become worthless. Issuers can and do become insolvent after successful fundraises. Returns are never guaranteed.
ul.i01: Illiquidity. Crowdfunded and tokenized positions can be hard or impossible to sell. There may be no secondary market, transfers can require the issuer's or platform's consent and a verified recipient, and you may have to hold until the project ends - or longer. (On the current prototype no transferable token exists at all.)
ul.i02: Subordination. Subordinated or "junior" instruments rank behind other creditors; with qualified subordination you may receive nothing while the issuer is over-indebted, and interest or repayment claims can be suspended entirely.
ul.i03: Term and extension risk. Loans and bonds may be extended beyond their stated term under their contracts, delaying repayment.
ul.i04: Valuation risk. Real-world assets are hard to value; stated valuations may be wrong or stale. (On this demo, all valuations and issuer identities are mock data.)
ul.i05: Smart-contract risk. Code can contain bugs or be exploited, and transactions on a blockchain are generally irreversible.
ul.i06: Network risk. Blockchain networks can suffer congestion, outages, forks or protocol changes outside anyone's control.
ul.i07: Key and wallet risk. If you lose your wallet's secret key or recovery phrase, or someone steals them, your funds are gone and no one can restore them.
ul.i08: Regulatory risk. Rules for crowdfunding (ECSPR in the EU) and crypto-assets (MiCA) are evolving. A structure that is possible today may change, and offerings may be restricted where you live.
ul.i09: Volatility and currency risk. Crypto-asset prices can move sharply; stablecoins can de-peg; exchange rates move.
ul.i10: Counterparty and fraud risk. Issuers may mismanage funds or misrepresent their projects. Platform checks reduce but cannot eliminate this.

b11.p: EU crowdfunding regulation (the ECSPR, Regulation (EU) 2020/1503) requires authorised platforms to offer investor categorisation, an entry knowledge test, a simulation of the ability to bear loss, and a pre-contractual reflection period of four calendar days for non-sophisticated investors before an offer becomes binding; the reference platforms in our research corpus implement these under their own authorisations. Blockallisto's demo has none of these mechanisms, because no real investment is possible. If a regulated version ever launches, those protections - and their limits - will be described in its own legally reviewed documents. Protections like reflection periods let you withdraw an offer; they do not reduce the underlying investment risk.

b13.p: Nothing on this Service is investment, legal or tax advice, or a recommendation to buy or sell anything. Past performance - real or simulated - does not predict future results. Consider independent professional advice, and diversify: do not concentrate your savings in any single project or asset type.

b15.p: By using this demo you acknowledge that you have read and understood this Risk Disclosure. Before any future real launch, a fuller, legally reviewed risk statement will apply.

b02.p: This policy template describes how Blockallisto intends to identify, prevent, manage and disclose conflicts of interest. Blockallisto today is a prototype demonstration on the Stellar testnet: there are no real investors, issuers, funds or offers, so no actual conflict can arise today. This document is a design artifact prepared against the compliance surfaces of established EU crowdfunding platforms and is not a description of a live compliance program.

b04.p: Crowdfunding platforms sit between issuers seeking funds and investors providing them. Regulation (EU) 2020/1503 expects authorised platforms to avoid conflicts of interest and, where they cannot be avoided, to manage and disclose them. This template anticipates that expectation.

ul.i00: Platform vs investor: the platform earning fees from completed raises could be tempted to admit weak campaigns. Intended mitigation: published admission criteria, documented due-diligence steps per campaign, and fees that do not depend on campaign marketing claims.
ul.i01: Related parties: the operator, its managers or their close relations acting as issuers or investors. Intended rule: [related parties may not act as issuers on the platform - to be confirmed by legal advice]; any related-party investing, if ever permitted, would be disclosed on the campaign page.
ul.i02: Proprietary investing: intended rule: the platform does not invest in its own campaigns and does not hold contributed funds at any point; settlement flows through [licensed payment service providers - planned, not live].
ul.i03: Staff incentives: intended rule: no remuneration tied to the funding success of specific campaigns.
ul.i04: Information asymmetry: issuer-supplied content could mislead. Intended mitigation: key investment information sheets per campaign, a standardised campaign data structure, and clear separation between verified platform data and issuer-supplied content.

b08.p: Intended process: (1) conflicts register maintained by [the operator's compliance contact - to be appointed]; (2) assessment before any campaign admission and on any material change; (3) where a conflict cannot be avoided, disclosure to affected users in clear terms before they commit; (4) refusal to operate the conflicting business where avoidance and disclosure are insufficient.

b10.p: None of the above is operative today. The prototype accepts no real funds, lists no real issuers and pays no fees. This page exists so the intended compliance surface is visible and reviewable before any real launch.

b02.p: This page explains how to complain about the Blockallisto prototype and how complaints are handled. Blockallisto today is a demo on the Stellar testnet with no real funds involved; the handling process below is real for the demo, while the formal regulatory framework it mirrors applies only to an authorised platform.

b04.p: Email {v:contactEmail} with the subject "Complaint". Include: what happened, when, the page or feature involved, and what outcome you are asking for. Complaints are free of charge.

b05.p: For the prototype there is also a support ticket form on the site; complaints sent there are handled the same way.

ul.i00: Acknowledgement: we confirm receipt within [10 business days - template value].
ul.i01: Investigation: the operator reviews the complaint against records (page content, contract events, support history). You may be asked for clarification.
ul.i02: Answer: a reasoned reply within [20 business days - template value] of acknowledgement. If more time is needed, we say so and explain why.
ul.i03: Record: complaints and outcomes are logged in a complaints register kept for [5 years - template value], containing the complaint, the investigation and the resolution.

b08.p: Template timelines are indicative values drawn from common EU platform practice, not legal commitments; final values require legal advice.

b10.p: For the prototype there is no supervisory escalation path, because the operator is not an authorised crowdfunding service provider and no real investment service exists. For a future authorised platform, this section will name the competent authority's complaint channel (in Portugal, the CMVM) and any applicable out-of-court dispute-resolution body before any real offer is made.

b12.p: Recurring complaint themes are reviewed and feed into product and content fixes. The prototype's own roadmap treats complaints data as an input to design changes, not just case-by-case resolution.

b02.p: This page describes what keeps the Blockallisto prototype available and recoverable, and what continuity planning is intended for a future authorised platform. The first section is factual about the running demo; the second is design intent, not current practice.

ul.i00: No client assets at risk: the demo holds no money, no client funds and no custody. Contributions are testnet tokens with no monetary value, settled by a Soroban smart contract on the public Stellar testnet. Contract state lives on the testnet ledger, independent of this website.
ul.i01: Hosting: the site and API run on Render's free tier; operational data (transaction journal, community data) lives in a Neon Postgres database on its free tier. Both are third-party services with their own availability properties; no uptime is guaranteed for the demo.
ul.i02: Backups: [backup schedule and retention to be defined - the free tiers provide no managed backups; testnet contract state is recoverable from the public ledger].
ul.i03: Staging separation: user-facing demo, a separate staging environment, and disposable database copies are kept apart so testing cannot corrupt the demo.
ul.i04: If the demo is unavailable: no user loses anything of value. Campaign state remains readable on public Stellar testnet explorers, and contributions remain governed by the contract, not by this site.

b05.h2: 2. Intended continuity plan for an authorised platform (not live)

b06.p: A real platform handling regulated offers would need, before launch: documented recovery time and recovery point objectives [RTO/RPO values to be set with legal and infrastructure advice]; managed backups with tested restore procedures; a payment-services arrangement in which client funds are never held by the platform, so platform failure cannot strand investor money; an orderly wind-down plan ensuring ongoing campaigns can complete or refund if the platform ceases operating; and communication procedures for incidents affecting users.

b07.p: None of this is operative today. Publishing it as a template keeps the intended compliance surface visible and reviewable.

b09.p: To report a security or availability incident affecting the prototype: {v:contactEmail}, subject "Incident".
